focus: Repository rules against Ponytail doctrine: gaps and already-stronger coverage
noveltyJustification: Three findings are fully new (diff decodability floor, move/merge behavior preservation, equal-cost edge-case tiebreak), two apply round-one or earlier-round ideas to rule targets (reach set, accessibility never-cut), and two reconfirm rules that already exceed Ponytail.
keyQuestions: Which Ponytail teachings improve the repository rules (.skilled/repo-rules/*.md) without weakening scope, evidence, verification or communication floors?
answeredQuestions: Which Ponytail teachings improve the repository rules (.skilled/repo-rules/*.md) without weakening scope, evidence, verification or communication floors?

ruledOut.approach: Port Ponytail's numbered ladder into the repository rules
ruledOut.reason: prevent-overengineering.md deliberately keeps a reversal-cost order and points to the code skill's ladder as the authority; a second numbered ladder creates rung ambiguity.

ruledOut.approach: Add Ponytail's one-small-test reflex to the rules
ruledOut.reason: Round one rejected it against the stronger P1 coverage floor, which prevent-overengineering.md already defers to.
scope-discipline.md explicitly blocks reading restraint as license to narrow the ask.

label: The reach set is only half-enumerated in the pre-write pass: Ponytail lists callers, tests, fixtures, config and exports, while prevent-overengineering.md Sec2 asks for the owning module, one real caller and the contract (the dangerous half) but not the rest. ALREADY-COVERED idea, NEW target.

The decodability floor for minimal diffs is absent: Ponytail says a one-liner that needs decoding is not short, while the repo settles size purely by reversal cost with no counterweight against unreadable golf. NEW for prevent-overengineering.md Sec1.

Moved or merged code is not required to keep its error handling and validation: Ponytail states the rule, while the rules only forbid deliberately cutting error handling and treat rename/move as mechanical in-scope changes. NEW for scope-discipline.md Sec2 or prevent-overengineering.md Sec5.

No tiebreaker for equal-cost options on edge-case correctness: Ponytail takes the option correct on edge cases when sizes tie, while the reversal-cost order breaks ties by cost only. NEW for prevent-overengineering.md Sec1.

Accessibility is absent from the rules never-cut set: Ponytail names it, the rules carry the request, error-handling and dependency floors, and the word appears in none of the 14 rule files. ALREADY-COVERED idea (round one), NEW target for the rules.

The root-cause doctrine already beats Ponytail's version: reproduce the exact symptom, locate the producer, trace its other consumers, fix at the source and re-run the failing check plus the whole gate. ALREADY-ADOPTED, no action.

Ponytail's closing gap-disclosure line is already required in stronger form: evidence-and-proof.md Sec10 requires a four-part close-out plus an explicit what-is-not-done statement, which sharpens the @code RETURN gap finding. ALREADY-ADOPTED at the rules layer.
